`auth.billing_provider: stripe` in app.yaml turns on a built-in mirror of the Stripe subscriptions of the app's own customers; `stripe` is the only provider. It adds three routes (404 without the key) and the tables `_benmore_subscriptions` and `_benmore_invoices`, which flow SQL can read. Creating the Checkout Session stays the app's flow (`flow_snippet`, with `mode: subscription`).

POST /api/_billing/webhook is the endpoint to register in Stripe. It verifies `Stripe-Signature` (5-minute window) with the signing secret in the env value STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET: 503 `billing webhook not configured: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var is missing` until that is set, 403 `invalid signature`, otherwise 200 `{"ok":true}`, also for event types it does not use. An event id is applied once, so a redelivery changes nothing.

Events it applies: `checkout.session.completed` ties the subscription to an app user; the session needs a customer, a subscription and `metadata.user_id` holding that user's id (set it from `${{ user.id }}` in the flow that creates the session). `customer.subscription.created`, `.updated` and `.deleted` store the status, the plan (the price's nickname, else its id), `current_period_end` and `cancel_at_period_end`. `invoice.payment_succeeded`, `invoice.payment_failed` and `invoice.finalized` store the invoice.

GET /api/_billing/me answers the signed-in caller's newest subscription, `{id, stripe_subscription_id, status, plan, current_period_end, cancel_at_period_end}`, or `{"status":"none"}`; signed out it answers 401.

POST /api/_billing/portal (signed in, with the CSRF token) opens a Stripe customer-portal session with the secret key in the env value STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and answers `{url}` to send the browser to. The body's `return_url` is optional: a path, or a URL on the app's own origin (400 otherwise). Without the key it answers 503 `billing not fully configured: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY env var is missing`, and 404 when the caller has no subscription yet.

`auth.billing_webhook_secret_env` and `auth.billing_api_key_env` name other env values for the two secrets (`billing_webhook_secret_env: PAY_HOOK_SECRET`). `auth.billing_publishable_key_env` has no effect (the page that loads Stripe.js holds its own `pk_` key), and the write gate and `benmore check` warn about it.
